summary: Average True Range: the 14-bar Wilder average of each bar's true range, a plain measure of how much price moves.
overview: The Average True Range (ATR) measures volatility in its own pane. A higher line means bars are moving more; a lower line means quieter trading. It does not show direction.
The line turns orange while ATR is expanding.
how: True range = the largest of: high - low, |high - previous close|, |low - previous close|. ATR = average of true range over 14 bars, smoothed with Wilder's RMA by default.
Other smoothing types can be chosen in the settings.
use: Some traders size stops as a multiple of ATR so they fit current volatility.
Use rising ATR to see when moves are getting larger.
Compare ATR with past readings to see if the market is calm or busy.
Use it to set position size so risk stays similar across symbols.
alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
ATR is in price units, so values differ across symbols.
